From: Lauren Price <lauren@finedge.com>

Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Pilot traffic spike — p50/p95 window ask

Hi Sean,

Quick one from our side as we ramp the pilot this week: we saw an unexpected client traffic spike overnight (attached CSV) that pushed a chunk of requests into longer-tail processing. Our product team is worried that your current measurement window + strict p95 commitment will trigger an SLA hit during the pilot — which would complicate our executive review.

Can Redwood temporarily relax the p95 measurement (or allow a one-week carveout) for this account while we stabilize load patterns? We're proposing: 1) a deterministic carveout window for the spike hours (03/20 03:00–06:00 UTC), or 2) a temporary adjustment to the p95 baseline for the pilot month. We can provide additional telemetry if that helps.

We'd like to avoid a full contract amendment; this is just a short-term operational exception while we complete autoscaling tweaks. If you need, I can loop procurement or legal.

Thanks —
Lauren

lauren@finedge.com

Hi Lauren — thanks for the heads up and for the CSV. I pulled this into the SRE queue and want to propose a pragmatic path forward that balances contract integrity with avoiding disruption to your pilot:

- Short-term fix: Redwood can apply a one-time measurement carveout for the spike window you listed (03/20 03:00–06:00 UTC). That will exclude those minutes from p50/p95 calculations for this week only.
- Operational guardrails: We'll require the telemetry package (SLO evidence) and an internal post-mortem outlining autoscaling changes.
- Timeline: carveout applied immediately upon acceptance; we will monitor for two business days.

If that works, I'll coordinate internally to ensure the carveout is recorded in the HubSpot deal and we issue a short memo for audit. CC'd Marissa to track contract/credits risk and Connor to handle the measurement change.

Short answer: we can do a temporary, narrowly-scoped carveout rather than changing the formal p95 commitment.

—Sean
